recent_posts.title: Building a witch marketplace with vibe coding and questionable math
recent_posts.summary: A satirical video/post documenting a tongue-in-cheek attempt to build a marketplace for witches and metaphysical services ('Taskrabbit for Witches') after Etsy banned such listings. The creator interviews a real witch shop owner, attends protests to sell protection spells, hands out candy at Supabase Conf to get signups, and extrapolates 10 signups in 2 hours into a projected $100K MRR. Features a cameo interview with Monzo/GoCardless founder Tom Blomfield discussing vibe coding. The content is comedic and satirical rather than a genuine business or technical tutorial.

recent_posts.title: Satirical skit about over-engineering a simple button in modern web dev
recent_posts.summary: A satirical skit lampooning the absurdity of modern software development culture, where shipping a simple button becomes an endless spiral of over-engineering. It mocks tech stack debates (Rust, microservices, Kafka, graph databases, service meshes), tooling obsessions (Vim, custom keyboards, Cursor vs VS Code), process theater (SAFe, Jira story points, RBAC for a button), and the constant churn of frameworks and trends. The punchline: after all the debate, nothing gets built.

recent_posts.title: Satirical tour through software architecture buzzwords and enterprise Java nostalgia
recent_posts.summary: A humorous, satirical rant cycling through a parade of software architecture buzzwords and patterns — microkernel, CRDT, event-driven microservices, ports and adapters, MVC, and more — poking fun at over-engineered systems, AI hype, and the absurdity of enterprise Java stacks like JBoss, WebLogic, and WebSphere. Ends with a tongue-in-cheek suggestion to skip code entirely and just draw UML diagrams or read O'Reilly books.

recent_posts.title: The absurd complexity of actually securing a VPS
recent_posts.summary: A satirical take on the overwhelming complexity of properly securing a VPS for a simple task. The piece humorously walks through the endless security steps required—hardening SSH, configuring firewalls, setting up VPNs, managing systemd services, and more—only to reveal the person is actually running everything on a local Mac Mini instead. It pokes fun at the gap between 'just use a VPS' advice and the reality of secure server administration.

recent_posts.title: Interview with a ‘Just use a VPS’ bro (OpenClaw version)
recent_posts.summary: A satirical dialogue highlighting the complexity and security challenges of setting up a VPS server. The piece walks through hardening SSH access, configuring firewalls, managing automatic updates, installing dependencies, and setting up systemd services—all while poking fun at the 'just use a VPS' mentality that oversimplifies server administration. The humor underscores how what seems like a simple one-click install actually requires extensive security configuration, system administration knowledge, and ongoing maintenance.

recent_posts.title: PART 2 - Interview with VP of Dying' Company [Corporate Edition]
recent_posts.summary: A satirical transcript exposing dysfunctional corporate practices including excessive bureaucracy, meaningless OKRs designed to never be fully achieved, multiple layers of unnecessary reporting structures, and management tactics that prioritize appearances over productivity. The piece critiques remote executives who create fear-based cultures, hold endless pre-alignment meetings, take credit for others' work, and maintain power through information hoarding while remaining disconnected from actual product development.

recent_posts.title: Satirical punishments for common development workflow failures
recent_posts.summary: A satirical take on overly strict code review practices and development workflows, presenting absurd punishments for common development issues like long build times, failing tests, and low code coverage. The humor escalates from mild inconveniences to increasingly ridiculous consequences, poking fun at elitist developer attitudes and perfectionist coding standards.

recent_posts.title: The buzzword enthusiast in every tech meeting
recent_posts.summary: A humorous dialogue depicting a common tech meeting scenario where one participant repeatedly suggests buzzword solutions like microservices, Kubernetes, and Rust regardless of context, while others try to have a productive discussion about refactoring and system improvements.

recent_posts.title: AI recommendation systems integrating advertising and sponsored content
recent_posts.summary: A satirical example demonstrating how AI recommendation systems might integrate advertising and sponsored content into their responses. The piece shows an AI providing movie recommendations that seamlessly transition into promotional content and purchase prompts, highlighting concerns about the commercialization of AI-generated recommendations.
